lockFileMaintenance.description: A direct pin moving does not move the transitive resolution behind it. Measured 14 Sep 2026: bumping `@octokit/core` to 7.0.8 left `@octokit/rest`'s own `^7.0.6` descriptor resolved at 7.0.6, so two copies of the module stood in one tree and `@octokit/plugin-throttling`'s `declare module "@octokit/core"` augmentation landed on the copy nothing constructed — `onRateLimit`'s parameters went implicit-any and the typecheck failed with four errors that named neither package. `yarnDedupeHighest` above fixes that case at bump time; this fixes the half no bump touches.

prHeader:
![CI](https://img.shields.io/badge/CI-passing-2ea44f?style=flat&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white) ![size](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-small-2ea44f?style=flat) ![proof](https://img.shields.io/badge/proof-bronze-cd7f32?style=flat)
👉 NextRead the change below, then land it on green CI.
RiskLow. One dependency moves to a pinned version and nothing else does. A breaking release fails this repository's own checks before the merge queue can take it.
Blast radiusEvery module in this repository that imports the package named in the table below. The checks on this pull request are the tested surface.
ProblemThis repository pins every dependency to an exact version, so a pinned version only moves when something moves it. Left alone it ages out of its own security and bug fixes. Renovate opened this on the schedule renovate.json sets, no ask.
SolutionRenovate proposes one pinned version bump, respecting the freshness floor in renovate.json and the seven-day npmMinimalAgeGate in .yarnrc.yml. The table below names what moved.
ProofBronze. The whole gate runs against the new resolution on every push to this branch: lint, typecheck, both test lanes and the coverage floor. Nothing here is a claim a reader has to take on trust — read the checks.
---

packageRules.description: A freshly published bad major/minor release is never proposed. Patch bumps carry the lowest regression risk of the three and sit on the repository-wide 7-day floor instead, which is `.yarnrc.yml`'s `npmMinimalAgeGate` and not a second opinion about risk.
sharp is pinned to a portal: protocol range (a local stub, see stubs/sharp) — never a registry package to update.

engines.node is a floor chosen beside .nvmrc, never a version to track: the global pin strategy would rewrite `>=24.11` to one exact release above the .nvmrc pin, and Yarn refuses to install on the pinned Node the moment it lands.

A GitHub Action stays on its major tag. The exact-pin rule is yarn.config.cjs's, written for npm dependencies the lockfile resolves; an action tag pinned to v4.4.0 has no lockfile behind it and only ages.

TypeScript's next major is not a version bump here. Every house gate reads the compiler through `typescript/ast` and `typescript/sync` behind the four seam files `typescript-import-seam` names, and `named-object-params` holds a whole Program through that server; the 6-to-7.1 move reshaped node types (a nameless BindingElement, a PropertyName where an Identifier was) across 57 files under `src/` and its decision stream had to be proven byte-identical before it landed. A major is that piece of work again, so it gets its own pull request rather than riding a dependency sweep. Reproduce the first half of it: `yarn add typescript@<next major> && yarn typecheck`.

turbo-stream's version is dictated by what React Router v7 ENCODES with, not by what is newest — `src/atlas/nxCloud/dataRoute.ts` decodes the client's own single-fetch payloads. MEASURED 14 Sep 2026: 3.2.1 is a ground-up rewrite with a different wire format whose decoder does not refuse a v2 payload, so the atlas would have recorded every Nx Cloud run family as empty. The witness already exists — the fixed-bytes case in `src/__tests__/unit/atlas/nxCloud/dataRoute.test.ts` fails `chunk.charCodeAt is not a function`. Reproduce: `yarn add turbo-stream@3 && yarn vitest run --config config/vitest/unit.ts src/__tests__/unit/atlas/nxCloud/dataRoute.test.ts`.

Bumping this client is an ATLAS REGENERATION, not a dependency bump, so it never rides an automated sweep. `src/atlas/datadog/generated/sdkLock.ts` pins the version, a SHA-256 over every compiled `apis/*.js` module and an operation census, and `tools/generateDatadogSurfaces.ts` REFUSES when any of them moves — by design, so that nobody regenerates 1,735 reviewed rows from whatever was installed that morning. Verified 14 Sep 2026 against 1.63.0: `v1: digest moved`. The bump belongs in a pull request that also re-reads the two pinned OpenAPI documents at the new release tag and re-grades the atlas with `slopweaver atlas doctor`.

These move as ONE or they do not move. Each `@googleapis/*` package carries its own `googleapis-common` range, and `googleapis-common` carries the `google-auth-library` whose `OAuth2Client` the `auth` option is typed against — `src/live/google/authClient.ts` imports that class from `googleapis-common` for exactly this reason. MEASURED 14 Sep 2026: `googleapis-common` alone at 9.0.4, while the four `@googleapis/*` packages sat at majors the freshness floor still held, installed a second `google-auth-library` and produced eight `private property 'redirectUri'` errors across the Gmail, Drive and Calendar doors. Grouped, one pull request either moves the whole set or moves none of it.

vitest and its coverage provider are one release train — `@vitest/coverage-v8` is pinned to the exact vitest version by peer dependency, so a split proposal is an install-time refusal rather than a version skew. `vite` is named here because vitest 5 is what makes it a non-optional peer at all, and it will become a direct devDependency the moment that major lands.

vitest's next major is held. MEASURED 14 Sep 2026 on 5.0.0: the integration lane's Cloudflare file goes from 24 passing to 22 failing, every failure `[Polly] [adapter:fetch] Recording for the following request is not found and recordIfMissing is false`. The global fetch IS patched — logging `globalThis.fetch` at client construction prints Polly's own wrapper — so this is cassette MATCHING under the new runner rather than a broken intercept, and the 22 `it.each` cases fail while the two plain `it` cases in the same file pass. One file of the lane's 28 is affected and the mechanism was not resolved; the only other route, re-recording, means calling the real Cloudflare account and rewriting a reviewed cassette, so this gets its own pull request. Reproduce: `yarn add -D vitest@5 @vitest/coverage-v8@5 vite@8 && yarn vitest run --config config/vitest/integration.ts src/__tests__/integration/cloudflare.test.ts`.

`site/`'s zod is the version nextra parses against, not the newest one. nextra-theme-docs 4.6.1 destructures `children` OUT of the Layout's props and then parses the REST against a `z.strictObject` that still declares `children: reactNode` as a required key (`dist/layout.js`, `dist/schemas.js`) — so every docs page depends on a missing `z.custom()` key being accepted. MEASURED 22 Sep 2026: 4.1.12 accepts it and `yarn build` in `site/` exits 0; 4.4.3 (#893) refuses it with `Invalid input: expected nonoptional, received undefined → at children` and the export dies. Every page fails, not three — the export bails on the first, so which pages the log names changes run to run. The `site` check was red on main from that bump until this pin. The root's own zod is unaffected and keeps tracking. Reproduce: set the resolution to 4.4.3, then `yarn install && yarn build` in `site/`. Lift this when nextra stops parsing a key it has already removed.

The octokit packages augment each other's module declarations, so a split resolution is a type error rather than a version skew — see the lockFileMaintenance note above for the measurement. Grouped so one pull request moves the whole set and `yarnDedupeHighest` has a single tree to collapse.

`site/`'s `shiki` draws the console's code blocks in the `@shikijs/themes` pair `site/lib/codeThemes.ts` builds, and the root pins the same `@shikijs/themes` so the root unit lane, which cannot see `site/`'s dependencies, measures every token colour the console draws (`site/__tests__/unit/theme.test.ts` fails when the three pins differ). Grouped so one pull request moves them together.
